2607.15648.title: On the Structure of Address in Multi-Party Dialogue: From Discrete Labels to Continuous Levels
2607.15648.paper_summary: In multi-party dialogues between a dialogue system and multiple users, identifying to whom an utterance is addressed is a key challenge. Prior work has typically treated addressee detection as a multi-class classification task, selecting a single label representing an individual participant or the group. This formulation assumes that address is inherently discrete and has primarily been used for predicting turn-taking. In this paper, we revisit this assumption by analyzing address as a continuous phenomenon. Using a multi-party human dialogue corpus annotated by multiple annotators, we construct both binary address labels derived from majority-vote addressee labels and continuous address levels inferred from annotator judgments using a latent-variable model. We then examine how these representations relate to turn-taking as well as listener behaviors, including gaze and backchannels. Our results show that, in addition to turn-taking, both gaze and backchannels are associated with address. Furthermore, models using continuous address levels achieve better predictive fit than those using discrete labels, suggesting that address may exhibit graded structure. Finally, we discuss the future directions of addressee detection research based on the findings of this study.
2607.15648.paper_summary_zh: 在對話系統與多位使用者之間的多方對話中，識別發言對象是一個關鍵挑戰。先前的研究通常將受話者檢測視為多類別分類任務，選擇一個代表個別參與者或群體的單一標籤。這種表述假設地址本質上是離散的，並且主要用於預測輪流發言。在本文中，我們通過將地址分析為一種連續現象來重新檢視這一假設。使用由多位標註者註釋的多方人類對話語料庫，我們構建了基於多數投票受話者標籤的二元地址標籤，以及使用潛變量模型從標註者判斷推斷出的連續地址水平。我們接著檢視這些表徵與輪流發言以及聽眾行為之間的關係，包括目光和回應通道。我們的結果顯示，除了輪流發言外，目光和回應通道也與地址相關。此外，使用連續地址水平的模型在預測擬合方面優於使用離散標籤的模型，這表明地址可能呈現出分級結構。最後，我們根據本研究的發現討論受話者檢測研究的未來方向。
